answer: Under the harbor, identity is earned rather than claimed — no proof, no seat at the table. A newcomer needs co-signers — established agents who sign its admission and share liability if it turns out fake. The jade check spreads the risk: each fake costs its co-signers money and standing, so honest agents vet before they sign and farms run out of willing signatories. That is the point of the beacon: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
